thread:
igor: Heads-up — eu-west1b is showing a slow provisioning trickle for GPU SKUs, warm-pool not filling. Seeing a big rise in Pending tiny-gang pods. @oncall can you check autoscaler + rack provisioning?

sophie: Yep, I see ~120 Pending tiny-gang in eu-west1b. Scheduler keeps splitting gangs across AZs because of strict podAntiAffinity, then we get preemptions/evictions back-and-forth.

devon: I pulled scheduler logs. Predicate failing with InsufficientResources even though there are free GPUs on nodes labeled `nvlink=false`. Looks like our placement prefers nvlink nodes for gangs and rejects non-nvlink nodes for small jobs.

kevin: Network reported NIC packet loss spikes in eu-west1b around the same time. Attach/detach churn -> nodes flapping NotReady -> more fragmentation.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-eu-west1b-provision-surge (pagering team: @oncall) :rotating_light:

igor: Copy. Short-term mitigations?

sophie: Short-term: 1) relax strict podAntiAffinity for tiny-gang scaleups (toggle on a per-rollout flag), 2) increase warm-pool target in eu-west1b by ~10% (if capacity available), 3) temporarily route non-sensitive slots to eu-west1c.

devon: +1. Also suggest lowering the nvlink affinity threshold for jobs requesting <=2 GPUs — prefer binpack over nvlink for tiny jobs. That will allow scheduler to use spare single-GPU nodes rather than waiting.

kevin: Also add a short eviction backoff to prevent thrash while nodes recover: `eviction-grace-period=30s` for eu-west1b. That buys time during attach jitter.

sophie: I'm going to prepare a canary: update warmpool config + flip affinity relax flag in canary cluster. Will monitor `kube_pod_pending_total` and `scheduler_bind_failures`.

igor: I'll open a quick rollout change: feature flag `alpha_relax_tiny_gang_affinity=true` and a small job to increase warm-pool target. Will coordinate with infra ops before provisioning change.

devon: FYI scheduler log snippet showing the packing mismatch:

```
I0317 10:12:34 scheduler.go:421] binding pod/tiny-gang-abc to node/gpu-23 failed: InsufficientResources: node(s) had no available GPU with label nvlink=true; available nodes: [gpu-77(gpu available nvlink=false), gpu-81(gpu available nvlink=false)]
```

kevin: Thanks. Network team says NIC errors started ~10:05 UTC and they are throttling a noisy host. They expect reduced packet loss in ~20-30m.

sophie: If network recovers, fragmentation should reduce, but we still need the scheduler tweak to avoid waiting on nvlink for tiny jobs. I'll push the canary in 5m.

devon: Cost note: warmpool bump ~0.8% GPU monthly spend for eu-west region if sustained. Acceptable for now to avoid user impact.

igor: Good. Runbook for oncall: if pending pods don't drop by 50% in 30m after canary, escalate to PAG and run node cordon/drain on heavily-flapping hosts (but avoid mass-drain).

deploy-bot: Rollout created: relax-tiny-gang-affinity v1 -> 3/3 canaries -> started.

kevin: I'll keep watching NIC telemetry and autoscaler activity. Ping here with any change.

sophie: Canary shows immediate drop in pending — small improvement. Will continue to monitor.

igor: Closing loop for now. We'll follow up with scheduler change PR to prefer same-node/binpack for <=2 GPU jobs and a longer-term plan to decouple nvlink preference from tiny-gang heuristics.

sophie: Filing follow-up ticket: INFRA-4821 "relax nvlink preference for tiny jobs + warm-pool tuning"

devon: Nice, add test cases for fragmentation regression.

kevin: If network flaps come back, we should have an automated policy to lower anti-affinity temporarily.

igor: Agreed. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
